How it runs

Side by side on the Mac mini

JIMBO-DJ · PORT 4490 · UNCHANGED

Keeps every write until it hands one over

  • Plex playlists and Fix in Plex
  • History imports and Plex scans
  • The analyzer posts its results here
  • Writes data/jimbodj.sqlite

read-only
mode=ro

TRAQFREQ · PORT 4491 · NEW REPO

Reads jimbo-dj, writes only its own

  • Opens jimbodj.sqlite as legacy, read-only
  • Its own database per module
  • Reuses jimbo-dj’s functions, pinned to a release
  • Same Tailscale, same Plex

1

One writer at a time. When a module cuts over (P6), traqfreq takes that write and jimbo-dj’s switch for it goes off in the same release.

traqfreq · build phases

Nothing in jimbo-dj changes for this build until a cut-over. traqfreq opens jimbo-dj’s database read-only through a read-only mount, so it can’t corrupt it, and it reuses jimbo-dj’s Python by depending on a tagged release instead of copying code early.

Nothing in jimbo-dj changes for this build until a cut-over. traqfreq opens jimbo-dj’s database read-only through a read-only mount, so it can’t corrupt it, and it reuses jimbo-dj’s Python by depending on a tagged release instead of copying code early.

How sessions work

One session, one window, one pull request

START · SMALL

Read only what the session needs

CLAUDE.md (one page), HANDOFF.md, and the one spec in docs/specs. No reading jimbo-dj beyond the functions it reuses.

BUILD · TESTED

Fixture database, not the real one

Tests run on a small generated copy of jimbo-dj’s schema, so cloud sessions never need your library.

END · HANDED OFF

Push, note, deck

Tests green, pull request open, HANDOFF.md says done and next, and this deck’s status and log are updated.

New chat at the start of each phase, or sooner when a chat grows long. The handoff note and this deck carry everything across.

On the Mac mini: from T2, sessions run in jimbos-sloppydrive/traqfreq on the Mac mini, driven from the laptop by Remote Control, so gates run in the same session.

traqfreq · build phases

Token-efficient by design: each session starts from a one-page CLAUDE.md, the handoff note and one spec, never from this long planning conversation. If a usage window runs low, the session stops at the last green commit and writes the handoff.

traqfreq · build phases

The file is the anchor: all three servers read the same music folder, so a track’s path below that folder names it everywhere. MusicBrainz IDs and tags stand in only where a server hides paths. No fingerprints: traqfreq never opens the audio. Jellyfin and Navidrome need their URLs and keys before T17 and T18. Writing playlists to them comes later, in the cut-overs.

Gate for each: a week with jimbo-dj’s switch off and nothing missed. Data that moved is copied once, checked by count, then traqfreq reads its own copy.

traqfreq · build phases

Each cut-over is one release of each app: traqfreq gains the write and jimbo-dj turns its version off. If a cut-over goes wrong, switch jimbo-dj’s back on; its data hasn’t been touched.

Each cut-over is one release of each app: traqfreq gains the write and jimbo-dj turns its version off. If a cut-over goes wrong, switch jimbo-dj’s back on; its data hasn’t been touched.

Phase P8 · Retire and skins

TO DO

P8

jimbo-dj retires; skins arrive

RETIRE · 2 SESSIONS

Switch off, keep the record

A final backup, jimbo-dj’s container stopped, its repo archived read-only. Playlists keep their emoji prefixes, so nothing in Plex changes.

SKINS · 3 SESSIONS

The other nine directions

Tokyo, New York, Zürich, Hong Kong and the rest become skins: token files you pick in SETUP. Same components, same copy.

LATER

Only when needed

A desktop companion (Tauri) for the analyzer; LIVE for setlists and concerts; a public release.

Gate: jimbo-dj stays off for a week with nothing missing in traqfreq.

traqfreq · build phases

Skins are cheap because of the token system: a direction is one JSON file over the same eleven components. London needs its own mark before it can ship, and Mexico City its own pictograms.
